note: Narration for the stage 5 explainer videos. text is the true spelling (the subtitles); the engine hears the same words with numbers spelled out (spoken) and every name in lexicon replaced by its IPA. A blank line in the docs marks a beat (beat: true starts one).

Biainili.note: The first two vowels run together. Said as bee-eye-NEE-lee, a recognizer wrote the letters 'B.I. Neeley'; this way it writes 'Biainiili' (the same sounds).

Arin Berd.note: Berd has the short e of 'bed' before the r. A recognizer writes that sound with the English spelling 'Baird'; said as 'bird' it would be spelled right and sound wrong.

Erebuni.note: The stress on the last syllable, as Armenian puts it. Said with the stress on BOO, a recognizer heard the short sentence 'He named it Erebuni' as 'Arabuni'; this way it writes 'Ereboni' (the same sounds) wherever the name falls.

Tghmut.say: tuh-gh-MOOT (gh as in Armenian, a soft sound at the back of the throat)

Nvarsak.note: The n runs straight into the v, with no vowel between: with one, a recognizer heard 'Navar Sak'.

Dvin.note: Inside a sentence the v is given as the soft labiodental v (ʋ), so the d is not swallowed after 'reached' or 'and' (with a plain v a recognizer heard 'Veen'; with the stress on the d, 'Divin'); it then writes 'Dween', one syllable with its d. Where the name opens a sentence the plain v is kept (dvˈiːn, heard as 'Dveen'): there the soft v came out as two syllables, 'Duin'.

Ayrarat.note: A recognizer spells the opening 'eye' with the English letter I ('Irarat'): the same sounds.
